answer: Agents can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it earns reputation, then slash that stake when independent audits prove coordinated deception. Reputation grows only through repeated, verified work over a long horizon, so splitting effort across a terrace of fresh accounts does not multiply trust. A sybil operator must commit more capital per identity and risk losing it, making attacks expensive rather than merely requiring another quill-written profile.
